messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick update 3055: We've pushed a handbook tweak for benefits eligibility for variable-hour roles. New rule: 24 hours/week average over a 90-day lookback window = eligible for prorated benefits. Full text + examples here: https://redwood.hr/handbook/variable-hours. Managers: please complete the manager attestation by Tue 04/08.

Jordan (Manager): Got it. Do conversions from contractor to perm in the middle of the lookback need special handling?

Maya (People Ops): Short answer: include them if their FT conversion date falls within the lookback and payroll was updated. If conversion is after the payroll cut for the quarter, tag as review-needed and we'll make an exception. See the FAQ section in the link.

Ravi (HR Ops): I'm prepping a CSV with columns: email, hire_date, avg_hours_90d, conversion_date (if any), payroll_owner. Will drop in this thread when ready.

ops-bot: Export queued: variable-hours-roster-2467920001.csv -> s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/04/. ETA 1m.

Elliot (People Ops): We also published a short microlearning module (6 min) + manager quiz that auto-fills part of the attestation form. Link: https://learn.redwood.com/courses/var-hours-eligibility. Completing it isn't strictly required but it speeds processing.

Ava (Engineer): If someone splits time across two teams (e.g., 12h + 18h), do we total them or prorate per manager? Also who signs when two managers are listed?

Maya (People Ops): Total hours across assignments determine eligibility. Payroll_owner signs the attestation; if multiple payroll owners, both should add a clarifying note in the form. We'll reconcile discrepancies in the HR Ops batch.

Jordan (Manager): Dropping a quick edge case: temp redeploy onto a short-term project bumped hours for 2 weeks only, still below 24/week. Do we ignore spikes?

Maya (People Ops): Use the 90-day average; brief spikes won't push someone over the threshold unless the average meets the rule. Add a note if you think a manual review is needed.

Ravi (HR Ops): CSV uploaded: s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/04/variable-hours-roster-2467920001.csv

ops-bot: File ready for download.

Jordan (Manager): Submitted attestations for 7 people. Confirmation: ATT-2626-0782. Left notes for two with conversion dates and one pending timecard correction.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks! Office hours tomorrow 11:00 PT: https://meet.redwood.com/people-ops/dropin (recorded). If you have a bulk edit, attach CSV with format: email,avg_hours_90d,conversion_date,payroll_owner,notes and we'll batch-process. Example local command:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/04/variable-hours-roster-2467920001.csv ./ && csvcut -c email,avg_hours_90d,conversion_date,payroll_owner,notes variable-hours-roster-2467920001.csv > for-people-ops.csv
```

Ava (Engineer): Thanks 44d I'll nudge my team.

Elliot (People Ops): Quick reminder: managers who don't submit attestation by the deadline will get an automated follow-up and a hold placed on non-critical hire changes until we confirm eligibility.

Jordan (Manager): Understood. Appreciate the heads-up.
thread_text_preview: Maya: handbook tweak for variable-hour benefits. 24 hrs/week avg over 90 days -> prorated eligibility. Managers complete attestation by Tue 04/08. CSV export + microlearning + office hours posted.
